subject: Zodiac13b elevated timeouts — recovery actions and post-incident commitments
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mendez <aisha.m@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: ops@quickcommerce.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zodiac13b elevated timeouts — short-term mitigations

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the alert this morning — we saw the elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting your production calls to zodiac13b. First, I want to apologize for the disruption. Our on-call and model-ops teams are the highest priority response right now.

What we've done so far (summary):
- Identified a spike in KV cache eviction rates correlated with a higher-than-usual long-prefix workload from a small percent of sessions.
- Deployed immediate routing rule for QuickCommerce traffic to a compatible zodiac13b-small fallback variant (lower context, preserved behavior) to reduce per-request memory pressure.
- Reduced default max_tokens for affected routes from 1024 to 512 and enabled a short-term batching cap to keep latency within your SLO.

Next steps we are executing:
1) Collect and analyze full traces (we've started pulling debug traces and attached a head snapshot).
2) Backfill missing KV snapshot data to avoid future cold-cache surges.
3) Work with model engineering to surface a quantization patch and a runtime memory fix for zodiac13b (ETA 72 hours).

Immediate ask: can you share (if possible) a few request IDs from the 08:30–09:00 window this morning so we can correlate? Sending anything private to ops@quickcommerce.com is fine.

I'll keep you updated every 6 hours while we work the recovery. Ben/Marissa/Karthik are cc'd for any commercial/credits coordination.

Apologies again — we know this impacts your user flows and we are treating it as Sev 1.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: DRAFT: Zodiac13b interim RCA and actions (for customer review)

Team — pulling together the internal draft RCA for review before we publish to QuickCommerce. Please keep this internal until we finalize the wording.

Timeline (concise):
- 08:18 PST — Noticeable error rate increases observed by customer metrics and internal SLOs.
- 08:23 PST — Internal alerts fire; on-call engaged.
- 08:34 PST — We confirmed elevated KV cache churn tied to a small set of long-prefix sessions; memory pressure cascaded to request timeouts on zodiac13b primary shards.
- 08:45 PST — Implemented routing to zodiac13b-small fallback and capped max_tokens; error rate reduced ~85% within 12 minutes.

Root cause (interim):
- Runtime memory growth under certain long-prefix request patterns triggered aggressive cache eviction; the eviction policy did not account for this new prefix distribution.

Corrective actions (short/medium term):
- Short-term: permanent routing rule for affected customer segments and update our runtime to evict less aggressively for long-prefix sessions (rolled in 6 hours).
- Medium-term: apply quantization-friendly patch + updated kernel selection for zodiac13b (engineering ETA: 48–72 hours).
- Long-term: extend automatic prefix classification to detect and pre-warm KV caches for heavy-tail prefixes.

Operational commitments:
- Customer-facing postmortem within 48 hours of the incident closure with full traces where allowable.
- One-month credit proposal to be finalized with Ben and sent by end of week.

Attachments: zodiac-quant-patch.diff (internal), postmortem-draft-link: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/0Bzodiac13b-postmortem

Please reply with edits by EOD.

— Marissa
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Zodiac13b incident resolved — final update and postmortem link

Hi Aisha,

Quick update and closure from Redwood: the engineering and runtime teams have implemented the medium-term mitigations and verified stability for your traffic. Summary:
- The fallback routing remains in place while we complete a staged rollout of the quantization/runtime patch to zodiac13b.
- We deployed a patch that adjusts eviction thresholds for long-prefix sessions and a targeted kernel-selection change; both reduced memory pressure in our validation tests and in a canary for QuickCommerce traffic.
- Error rates for your production routes returned to baseline within ~30 minutes of the canary rollout; we've kept an elevated monitoring window for 72 hours.

What we are sharing now:
- Customer-facing postmortem (redacted traces and timeline): https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/0Bzodiac13b-postmortem
- Action items we will complete in the next 30 days: pre-warm for heavy prefixes, improve GV cache metrics to detect this earlier, and a follow-up on deterministic replay tooling.
- Commercial: we're preparing a one-month service credit tied to the measured error window (Ben will send the credit memo).

If you'd like a short walkthrough of the postmortem and the technical changes, we can schedule a 30-minute call next week — suggest Mon/Tue morning PST.

Again, sincerely sorry for the impact. We're tightening our instrumentation and rollout checks to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
